title: SMB Quickstart Pack — Pricing & Onramp Playbook
content:
Summary:

This playbook describes the 'SMB Quickstart Pack', a compact offering and onboarding path for small and early-stage customers who want fast time-to-value, predictable costs, and little operational overhead. It covers the product overview, minimum viable requirements (PRD), integration design constraints, a staged launch roadmap, pricing and packaging, a release notes checklist for field teams, and a runbook-style onboarding flow.

Goals:
- Bring time-to-first-successful-integration under 3 days for typical developer workflows.
- Give a clear mapping from consumption to cost, with predictable monthly pricing and optional usage tiers.
- Ship guards out of the box that protect platform SLOs: 99.5% request success, p95 latency < 250ms for token generation under typical usage profiles.
- Offer a self-serve upgrade path to Dedicated/Private.

Target customers and personas:
- Product and engineering teams at SMBs and startups with 1–10 engineers.
- Primary personas: CTO/Founding engineer (buyer), Lead engineer (integration), Product manager (prioritization).

Quickstart pack components (what is included):
1) Developer toolkit (self-serve):
   - SDK starter repo (Node, Python) with sample prompts and a small demo app.
   - Preconfigured Redwood Console telemetry dashboard template (token-cost, per-route latency, errors).
2) Cost & SLO presets:
   - Default batching and cache profiles tuned for low-burst SMB workloads.
   - Safety caps (per-tenant tokens-per-minute limits) and automatic throttling policies.
3) Prebaked prompts and evals:
   - 3 starter prompt-sets for common use cases (summarization, support triage, code assist) and a lightweight eval harness.
4) Onboarding credits and migration path:
   - 30-day trial with $200 usage credit and 10k free embedding units.
   - Direct upgrade link to Dedicated with a migration checklist.

MVP requirements (product requirement checklist):
- PRD-001: Self-serve sign-up that provisions a tenant with the default Quickstart policy.
- PRD-002: One-click SDK scaffold (Python/Node) with a sample app that authenticates and calls the Redwood API.
- PRD-003: Console experience with a prebuilt dashboard template and a preconfigured cost alert (alert at 70% credit consumption).
- PRD-004: Cost caps and throttles: per-tenant rate limit at 5 requests/s and 10k tokens/min by default.
- PRD-005: Telemetry tags route, model_variant, and tenant_id present for all Quickstart tenants.
- PRD-006: Billing integration: usage tagged to the Quickstart SKU for credit consumption.

Acceptance criteria:
- 90% of test customers finish the sample integration (token exchange + first generation) within 3 days.
- No Quickstart tenant degrades average p95 latency by > 5% across the hosted pool over a 7-day window.
- Billing reconciliation attributes Quickstart usage correctly for 100% of test transactions.

Design constraints and engineering notes:
- Service boundary: Quickstart runs entirely on Hosted (no Dedicated routing by default).
- Runtime profile: small batches (max_batch_size=8); KV cache warmup off initially to keep the memory profile predictable.
- Telemetry hooks: metrics go to the 'quickstart' telemetry namespace with tags tenant_id, route, model, variant, billing_sku.
- Security: default tenant role "developer-quickstart" with a scoped API key and no access to private deployment features.
- Fallback policy: requests over soft limits get HTTP 429 with an 'x-retry-after' header; after 3 consecutive 429s the route is flagged for opt-in support outreach.

Sample configuration snippet (for the SDK starter README):

# Quickstart client config (YAML)
api_key: "<REDACTED>"
model: "redwood-compact-1"
max_tokens: 512
batch_profile: "quickstart-small"
telemetry:
  enabled: true
  namespace: "quickstart"

(Developer Experience will ship this file in the starter repos.)

Roadmap & launch milestones (quarterly view):
- Q3 2026 (MVP): self-serve flows, SDK scaffold, console dashboard, billing tagging, trial credits.
- Q4 2026: templated prompt library, lightweight eval harness, upgrade path to Dedicated.
- Q1 2027: localized docs (EU, APAC), automated migration assistant for Dedicated customers, partner reseller packaging.

Pricing & packaging (recommended tiers):
- Quickstart Basic (monthly): $49/mo
  - Includes 30k tokens/month, developer SDK, console template, community support.
  - Overages: $0.0008 per token beyond the included quota.
- Quickstart Pro (monthly): $199/mo
  - Includes 300k tokens/month, 10k embedding units, email support, 24-hour ticket SLA.
  - Overages: $0.0006 per token; preemptible warm capacity option +10% on request.
- Quickstart Growth (monthly commitment): $999/mo (discounted annual)
  - Includes 1.5M tokens/month, 100k embedding units, onboarding call, shared success manager.
  - Overages: $0.00045 per token; migration credit to Dedicated (up to $2k) on annual upgrade.

Packaging rules & constraints:
- Every Quickstart plan includes the 30-day trial offer once per account.
- Migration credit is additive and must be used within 90 days of moving to Dedicated.
- Pro-rated refunds follow standard billing policy; exceptions need finance approval.

Release notes (for product & sales):
- v0.9 (2026-08-24): Quickstart Basic & Pro tiers defined, SDK starter repos staged, console dashboard template available to pilot tenants, trial credit code generation enabled.
- Known limitations: no Dedicated routing from Quickstart by default; KV cache disabled for memory predictability; EU data residency not available in MVP.

Customer onboarding play (step-by-step):
1) Customer signs up and gets a Quickstart tenant plus trial credits.
2) Customer follows the Quickstart README and runs the sample app (CLI: `npm run quickstart` or `python -m quickstart`).
3) After the sample works, nudge the team to import one prompt set and turn on the console dashboard.
4) At 70% credit consumption an automated email recommends a SKU upgrade.
5) Above 1M tokens/month, share the Dedicated migration checklist and offer migration credit.

Runbook: Operational escalation (SRE + Product)
- Tenant causes sustained p95 latency > 250ms for 10 minutes: batch concurrency is reduced automatically and the owner notified.
- Billing tag failures above 0.1% of events in 24h: block new Quickstart signups and page Billing on-call.
- Trial credit consumption spikes > 5x expected: throttle, open a support ticket, and alert the product team to check for prompt abuse.

Ownership and contacts:
- Product (owner): Priya Patel — product strategy, roadmap, pricing.
- DevEx (owner): Diego Morales — SDKs, starter repos, README, onboarding flows.
- Console (owner): Anika Rao — dashboard templates, alerts.
- Billing & Finance: Liam O'Connor — pricing rules, credits, reconciliation.
- SRE: on-call rotation (see /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks for paging).

Risk, mitigations and open questions:
- Risk: Quickstart tenants may bring high-cost generative workloads that hurt pool economics.
  - Mitigation: conservative default caps, automated throttles, early cost-signal telemetry tagging.
- Risk: confusion between Quickstart and Dedicated feature sets.
  - Mitigation: in-console banners and an explicit 'Upgrade to Dedicated' flow with migration checklist.
- Open question: should Pro get limited KV cache? (Action: Product + Runtime to provide memory profile estimates by 2026-08-31.)

Appendix: Sample outreach template for sales/CS after 70% credit consumption:

Subject: Quickstart usage: recommend next steps
Hi <Customer>,

Your team is getting good use out of the Quickstart pack — you’ve used 72% of your trial credits. For predictable costs and more throughput, we’d suggest Quickstart Pro or starting a Dedicated evaluation. Happy to set up a 30-minute session to go through usage patterns and migration options.

Best,
<Success Manager>
